claims.claim: Visa counts Interlink and PLUS-branded transactions within its processed-transactions metric, confirming both are Visa-operated brands in FY2025.
claims.quote: represent transactions using cards and other form factors carrying the Visa, Visa Electron, V PAY, Interlink and PLUS brands processed on Visa's networks.
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K, fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: interlink|plus. Owner: Visa Inc. (HQ San Francisco per DOJ complaint caption). No ownership change since 2020. Visa reports Interlink volume inside consumer debit ('Includes consumer prepaid volume and Interlink volume'); no separate Interlink or PLUS card, transaction or ATM counts are published in the 10-K.

claims.claim: Visa describes the Visa/PLUS Global ATM network as providing cash access to debit, credit and prepaid account holders.
claims.quote: The Visa/PLUS Global ATM network also provides debit, credit and prepaid account holders with cash access and other banking capabilities.
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K, fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: plus. ATM count and country count not published in the 10-K.

claims.claim: Plus/Visa ATM acceptance is enabled through issuing and acquiring partnerships with financial institutions and independent ATM operators (IADs), i.e. non-bank deployers participate via a sponsoring member.
claims.quote: Issuing and acquiring partnerships with both financial institutions and independent ATM operators enable these capabilities.
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K, fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: plus. Partner types: issuer, ATM acquirer, independent ATM operator (via sponsor).

claims.claim: Mastercard's FY2025 10-K still lists Maestro and Cirrus as active brands in its brand family, with no mention of the Maestro phase-out.
claims.quote: including our primary brand Mastercard®, as well as our Maestro® and Cirrus® brands.
claims.title: Mastercard Incorporated Form 10-K, fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: maestro|cirrus. Owner: Mastercard Incorporated (Purchase, NY). No ownership change since 2020. The 10-K text contains no 'phase out' or retirement language for Maestro.

claims.claim: Mastercard defines Maestro as its PIN-based global debit solution and Cirrus as its primary global cash-access (ATM) solution.
claims.quote: Maestro (our PIN-based solution that operates globally) and Cirrus (our primary global cash access solution).
claims.title: Mastercard Incorporated Form 10-K, fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: maestro|cirrus. Role statement; single-message PIN debit (Maestro) and ATM (Cirrus).

claims.claim: Mastercard excludes Maestro and Cirrus cards and volume from its reported gross dollar volume, so no public volume, card or transaction figures exist for either brand.
claims.quote: Excludes Maestro and Cirrus cards and volume generated by those cards.
claims.title: Mastercard Incorporated Form 10-K, fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: maestro|cirrus. Absence finding: GDV and switched-transaction growth footnotes both exclude Maestro and Cirrus.

claims.claim: Mastercard switches substantially all cross-border Maestro and Cirrus transactions and earns cross-border volume and switching fees on them.
claims.quote: We switch substantially all cross-border transactions using Mastercard, Maestro and Cirrus-branded cards and generate a significant amount of revenue from cross-border volume fees
claims.title: Mastercard Incorporated Form 10-K, fiscal year ended December 31, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: maestro|cirrus. Also: 'We switch more than 70% of all transactions for Mastercard and Maestro-branded cards'.

claims.claim: Mastercard began phasing out Maestro in Europe on July 1, 2023, requiring European issuers to replace expiring or lost Maestro cards with a different product.
claims.quote: On July 1, 2023, Mastercard began phasing out Maestro across Europe.
claims.title: Maestro (debit card) - Wikipedia
claims.label: Reported
claims.note: network: maestro. Third-party source used because mastercard.com returned HTTP 403 to all fetches. Wikipedia infobox: 'Discontinued July 1, 2023 (few European countries only)'. The 2027 run-off end date named in the task brief could NOT be verified from a fetched source; Mastercard's October 2021 press release is behind a bot wall.

claims.claim: The DOJ complaint describes Interlink as Visa's back-of-card (PIN) debit network typically placed on Visa-branded debit cards alongside an unaffiliated network.
claims.quote: will often include Interlink, Visa's back-of-card network, and at least one additional back-of-card network that is not affiliated with Visa.
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: interlink. Filed September 24, 2024, before Capital One's May 18, 2025 acquisition of Discover/PULSE.

claims.claim: The DOJ complaint states Mastercard-branded debit cards typically carry Maestro plus at least one unaffiliated back-of-card network, confirming Maestro's continued US PIN-debit role in 2024.
claims.quote: Mastercard-branded debit cards typically include Maestro and at least one additional back-of- card network that is unaffiliated with Mastercard.
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: maestro. Complaint also says: 'Mastercard launched a PINless program for Maestro targeted at Visa-branded debit cards. But any gains were short lived.'

claims.claim: DOJ alleges that all PIN networks combined (Interlink and Maestro included in the back-of-card set) carry only about 11% of US debit transactions and 5% of card-not-present debit.
claims.quote: Collectively, the PIN networks represent approximately 11% of all debit transactions (and only 5% of card-not-present debit transactions).
claims.title: Complaint, United States v. Visa Inc., 1:24-cv-07214 (S.D.N.Y.)
claims.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: interlink|maestro. DOJ allegation, not adjudicated fact; complaint adds 'No PIN debit network has more than a single-digit share'.

claims.claim: On June 23, 2025 the S.D.N.Y. court denied Visa's motion to dismiss the DOJ debit monopolization case, and the opinion identifies Interlink and Maestro as the two network-affiliated back-of-card networks.
claims.quote: Visa and Mastercard each operate an affiliated back of card network: respectively, Interlink and Maestro.
claims.title: Memorandum Opinion and Order, United States v. Visa Inc., 24-cv-7214 (JGK), Dkt. 89
claims.publisher: U.S. District Court, S.D.N.Y. (Judge John G. Koeltl) via justice.gov
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: interlink|maestro. Conclusion text: 'Visa's motion to dismiss the complaint is denied.' Case remains in litigation as of the Visa FY2025 10-K (2025-11-06).

claims.claim: The June 2025 opinion recounts DOJ's allegation that in 2023 Chase sought a Visa waiver to enable both Maestro and PULSE on Visa debit cards to comply with the Reg II 2023 amendment (dual unaffiliated routing for CNP).
claims.quote: waiver to issue Visa debit cards with both Maestro and Pulse enabled, as required to comply with the 2023 Amendment.
claims.title: Memorandum Opinion and Order, United States v. Visa Inc., 24-cv-7214 (JGK), Dkt. 89
claims.publisher: U.S. District Court, S.D.N.Y. via justice.gov
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: maestro. Reg II status: Maestro is a routing-eligible unaffiliated network for Visa-issued cards; allegation as pleaded, not proven.

claims.claim: DOJ's case page lists the filed documents and confirms the case opened September 24, 2024 with the opinion added June 23, 2025.
claims.quote: Memorandum Opinion and Order (June 23, 2025) United States' Opposition to Visa Inc.'s Motion to Dismiss [Redacted] (January 19, 2025) Complaint (September 24, 2024)
claims.title: U.S. v. Visa, Inc. [2024] | Antitrust Division
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: interlink. Page footer 'Updated July 7, 2025'. Market listed as 'Credit and debit card networks'.

claims.claim: Visa's 10-K records the DOJ suit filing on September 24, 2024 and the denial of Visa's motion to dismiss on June 23, 2025, plus a wave of follow-on merchant and cardholder debit class actions from October 1, 2024.
claims.quote: On June 23, 2025, the court denied a motion to dismiss filed by Visa.
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K, fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: interlink. Same section: 'Beginning on October 1, 2024, several putative class actions were filed against the Company'. Earlier DOJ CID (March 13, 2012) 'focused on PIN-authenticated Visa Debit'.

claims.claim: Cardtronics filed an opt-out complaint against Visa and Mastercard on August 20, 2025 over the ATM access-fee non-discrimination rule that governs Visa/Plus (and Cirrus/Maestro) ATM transactions.
claims.quote: On August 20, 2025, Cardtronics USA, Inc., filed an opt-out complaint against Visa and Mastercard in the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K, fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: plus|cirrus. National ATM Council class action pending since October 2011; class certified August 4, 2021.

claims.claim: Visa's rule challenged in the ATM access-fee litigation bars ATM operators from surcharging a Visa or Plus transaction more than transactions on other networks.
claims.quote: if an ATM operator chooses to charge consumers an access fee for a Visa or Plus transaction, that fee cannot be greater than
claims.title: Visa Inc. Form 10-K, fiscal year ended September 30, 2025
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: plus. Visa notes 'a similar Mastercard rule' (Cirrus). Rule is a pricing constraint on ATM deployers, not a published fee.

claims.claim: Visa publishes a separate Interlink interchange schedule; consumer exempt retail is 0.80% + $0.15 and regulated (Reg II) debit is 0.05% + $0.21, rates effective July 1, 2023.
claims.title: Interlink Interchange Reimbursement Fees
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: interlink. Schedule header: 'Rates Effective July 1, 2023'. Columns: Exempt Consumer Interlink | Exempt Business Interlink | Regulated Interlink. Supermarket exempt consumer is flat $0.30; fuel exempt capped at $0.95. Also a Non-Visa BIN card-not-present table (e.g. Interlink Retail 2 CNP 0.65% + $0.15, $2.00 cap).

claims.claim: Interlink pays regulated issuers an extra $0.01 per transaction (the Reg II fraud-prevention adjustment) when they certify compliance with fraud standards.
claims.quote: Issuers that certify to Visa their compliance with the interim fraud prevention standards will receive an additional US $0.01 per transaction.
claims.title: Interlink Interchange Reimbursement Fees
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: interlink. Reg II status: Interlink is a covered network with regulated-rate column. Interlink rates are NOT in the main 'Visa USA Interchange Reimbursement Fees' PDF dated 18 April 2026 (zero matches).

claims.claim: Federal Reserve Reg II data for 2024 lists Interlink as a single-message network with an average interchange fee of $0.27 (0.59%) across all transactions and $0.25 (0.48%) on covered transactions.
claims.title: Regulation II - Average Debit Card Interchange Fee by Payment Card Network
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: interlink. Columns: exempt % count, exempt % value, exempt avg txn, exempt avg fee, exempt %; covered % count, covered % value, covered avg txn, covered avg fee, covered %; all avg txn, all avg fee, all %. claims.claim: Federal Reserve Reg II data for 2024 lists Maestro as a single-message network with an average interchange fee of $0.23 (0.55%) across all transactions, 74.9% of its transactions being covered.
claims.title: Regulation II - Average Debit Card Interchange Fee by Payment Card Network
claims.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: maestro. Confirms Maestro still reported as a live US single-message debit network for calendar 2024. Cirrus and Plus (ATM-only) do not appear because the table covers purchase transactions.

claims.claim: Under the Visa Rules, an issuer adds Plus ATM functionality by licensing the Plus Program Marks and providing 24x7 authorization.
claims.quote: To issue a Card with Plus functionality, an Issuer must do all of the following: l Obtain a license to use the Plus Program Marks
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, 18 April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: plus. Section 6.1.1.1 Plus Program Issuer Participation (ID# 0004060). Second bullet: 'Provide Authorization service 24 hours a day, 7 days a week'.

claims.claim: Any member-owned, leased, sponsored or controlled ATM may join the Visa Global ATM Network; members sponsoring non-member ATM agents must bind them to third-party agent and VisaNet processor contract rules.
claims.quote: Any ATM owned, leased, sponsored, or controlled by a Member is eligible for participation in the Visa Global ATM Network.
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, 18 April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: plus. Section 6.2.3.1. Glossary: 'Visa Global ATM Network The network through which an ATM participant provides Cash Disbursement services to Cardholders by acting as an Issuer, an ATM Acquirer, or both.' Also 'Proprietary Network A network owned and operated by a single Plus ATM Member'.

claims.claim: Interlink is governed by its own bylaws and rulebooks (Interlink Network, Inc. Bylaws, Interlink Core Rules, Interlink Product and Service Rules) that are referenced but not included in the public Visa Rules PDF.
claims.quote: as specified in the Interlink Network, Inc. Bylaws, Interlink Core Rules and Interlink Product and Service Rules, and the Visa Rules.
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, 18 April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: interlink. Glossary 'Interlink Program' (ID# 0024737): 'A program through which an Interlink participant (acting as an Interlink issuer) provides Point-of-Transaction services to Interlink cardholders, Interlink merchants, or both'. Plus likewise has 'Plus Core Rules and Plus Product and Service Rules'. Interlink appears 26 times in the 923-page PDF, mostly in marks and chip-AID rules.

claims.claim: Visa licenses the Interlink and Plus marks to members as part of the Visa-owned marks licence tied to the Visa programmes they hold, and maintains a Client Directory listing Interlink and Plus members and processors.
claims.quote: Visa grants to each Member a non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use each of the Visa-Owned Marks, including Interlink and Plus
claims.title: Visa Core Rules and Visa Product and Service Rules, 18 April 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: network: interlink|plus. Section 2.3.1.1 (ID# 0008906). Glossary 'Client Directory' names 'Visa, V PAY, Plus, and Interlink Members and processors'; Appendix A lists 'V.I.P. System SMS Interlink Client Implementation Guide' and 'Full Service Interlink Online Messages Technical Specifications' as member documents. Rules require Visa-owned AID transactions in the US to be processed 'as a Visa Transaction, a Visa Electron Transaction, an Interlink Transaction, or a Plus Transaction'.
